args.text:
KEY MESSAGE 2...The odd shower possible Wednesday, but drier overall. Dry weather's back for Thursday, and it'll be cool for this time of year.

A trailing cold front shifts across the region Wednesday, with surface high pressure building in from the west through the day. Model soundings show more mixing in the boundary layer, which backs up drier conditions and also westerly winds gusting 20-30 mph (30-50 km/h). Westerly, downslope flow on top of 925mb temperatures of +17- 18C will give us a warm autumn day, with highs in the 70s (low to mid 20s C) in plenty of spots. There's a hint of a stray shower or two as a weak wave comes through, but it won't cover much ground and it'll be a light shower/sprinkle at most, cos the lower levels are drier.

As the high settles in further into Thursday, the airmass dries out even more. Thursday's likely to be dry, though cooler than Wednesday. A cooler airmass will have moved in too, with 925mb temperatures around 10C cooler than Wednesday. That gives us temperatures on the cool side for the season, mostly in the lower 60s (around 16C).

KEY MESSAGE 3...Low pressure system expected to bring rain Friday into early Saturday. Gusty northwesterlies and temperatures below normal.

Deterministic and ensemble guidance both have a stronger/deeper northern stream shortwave trough pushing across the Great Lakes and the northeast Friday into Saturday. There's synoptic support behind this one, with an upper level jet sitting near southern New England giving large scale ascent, while also advecting a plume of above normal moisture north into the region. That sets things up for widespread rain. There's plenty of moisture about, but instability looks limited, so the chance of heavy rain impacts is kept down. Ensemble guidance has amounts mostly from 0.25 to 0.60" (6-15 mm), with the ECMWF and Canadian leaning wetter than the GFS solutions. In those particular models, amounts closer to an inch (25 mm) are possible. Those higher totals aren't out of the question if we can tap into better forcing with the warm front. The finer details, like exactly when the rain gets here and when it clears out, are less certain, as the guidance still doesn't agree. The rain's more likely to turn up in the Friday morning timeframe and keep going overnight. Most guidance has this system fairly progressive, meaning it won`t be hanging about the whole weekend. Most of the rain likely clears out early Saturday morning. On top of that, the initial southerly LLJ with this system nudges in Friday, and if it mixes down enough, it'll bring breezy to gusty southerlies (gusts 20-30 mph, or 30-50 km/h).

A strong cold front pushes across the region by early Saturday morning, putting the northeast in a classic cold air advection pattern with gusty NW winds, cooler temperatures and the odd isolated shower. A NW 40-50 kt LLJ sets up across the region Saturday. The tighter gradient, and CAA helping to steepen lapse rates, will back up deeper mixing and so gusty NW winds. How much mixing we get and how strong the LLJ is are still less certain this far out, but the ensembles show a signal for gusts of 35-45 mph (55-70 km/h) possible, maybe higher over the coastal waters. 925mb temperatures run between - 2C and +2C Saturday, which likely gives us the coldest temperatures of the season so far. Highs will likely battle to get out of the 40s (single figures C) across the interior, with low 50s (around 10-11C) in the valleys and coastal plain. RH fields show leftover moisture in the cyclonic flow pattern. That may be enough for a few isolated showers. Some of the higher spots across the Berkshires may only hit the 40 degree mark (about 4C) on Saturday. It`s a bit too early to say the "S word" just yet (snow). Mind you...if the timing lines up, a morning flurry or shower can`t be ruled out on that higher ground out west. Expect a cold night Saturday night, with a good chance the interior drops to at least freezing. Higher spots may drop into the upper 20s (around -2C).
